newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal hopes to privatise Mozambique dam - paper.
newsitem.headline: Portugal hopes to privatise Mozambique dam - paper.

text.p: Portugal's government hopes to privatise its majority stake in the Cahora Bassa dam in northern Mozambique and a senior Portuguese official will discuss the issue in Pretoria today, Publico newspaper reported.
South Africa controls the distribution of electricity from the dam in the Zambezia region of Mozambique, which is expected to come on stream in August this year, Publico said.
The paper said it had learned that Portuguese Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs Jose Lamego would discuss the matter with South African Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad.
Portugal's 82 percent stake in the dam is estimated to be worth 450 billion escudos, Publico said.
The government of Mozambique, a former Portuguese colony which owns the remaining 18 percent stake in the dam, backs the privatisation, it added.

The Socialist government of Prime Minister Antonio Guterres hopes to complete the privatisation by the year 2000 and would use the revenues to amortise public debt and help finance Portuguese projects in Mozambique, Publico said.
Portuguese government officials were not immediately available to comment on the newspaper report.
